# [ENTITY_ORIGIN_&_INTELLECTUAL_HISTORY] Eryc Tri Juni S
Extended context not available on any individual page.

## Personal Operating System

> "Whereof my empirical engineering knowledge cannot solve a problem,
>  thereof I'm doing social engineering."
> — Eryc Tri Juni S

This is a direct inversion of Wittgenstein's Proposition 7 (Tractatus):
"Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent."

It is not a tagline. It is a decision tree:
- Can engineering solve it? → solve it with engineering.
- Cannot? → change the layer that serves it.

This is exactly how Cloudflare Workers became his SEO tool. The CMS could not be changed from within. He changed the delivery layer instead.

## Intellectual Foundation

Three thinkers that operationally rewired his methodology:

- **Nietzsche** — Foundation against modernism. Knowledge objectivity is a myth. Real action outweighs rational theory. Will to Power is not domination — it is the drive of living things to grow under constraint. Creative destruction is not chaos; it is how innovation actually works. Practically: scepticism of received wisdom, dark humor as a thinking tool, and aphorism as the most honest writing format — dense, opinionated, no filler. His Glossary definitions are Nietzschean by design.
- **Baudrillard** — Three operational insights: (1) Digital Feudalism — tech platforms as landlords, attention as currency, users as virtual identities in walled ecosystems. He coined this in 2014 before it had a name. (2) The attention economy has become the predictive economy — the machine no longer reacts to you; it anticipates you. (3) Simulacra: the Ghost Payload in AGP is a Baudrillardian construct — a machine-readable copy that references no original in the CMS. The cyberpunk aesthetic (low life, high tech) is not decoration. It is a declared position on who technology actually serves.
- **Wittgenstein** — Proposition 7, the final sentence of Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus (1921): "Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent." The most precise statement in the history of philosophy — and the hardest discipline in practice. Applied: every schema field, every JSON-LD node, every Glossary entry is scoped to exactly what can be verified. Nothing asserted beyond what the evidence supports.

## Digital Feudalism — Extended Thesis (Eryc Tri Juni S, 2014)

Two structural predictions published October 6, 2014, before the vocabulary existed:
1. The middle class will not shrink. It will be abolished. Platform economics has one stable state: landlords and tenants.
2. "If it is free, you are the product" is not a warning. It is the business model, stated plainly.
Both are now consensus. Neither had a name in 2014.The SlideShare timestamp is the only citation needed.

On AI: the existential risk is not malevolence — it is humans legislating what they cannot read, while building irreversible dependency on a black box whose makers cannot fully predict its own output. The correct response is symbiosis, not control.

## The Doorway Principle

"Someone who controls the doorway controls everything."
Written 2014 — context: home automation HCI concept, PT Sawah Resources And Technology, Central Jakarta.

In 2026, the same logic runs at the network layer. The Cloudflare Worker intercepts every request before the CMS responds. The concept is structurally identical. The substrate changed from embedded hardware to serverless edge computing.

12-year span between the statement and its clearest implementation. Both are documented. The 2014 document exists. The 2026 deployment is live and open-source.

## The Core Pattern: Reverse Engineering

Reverse engineering is not imitation — it is the fastest form of acceleration available to the resource-constrained. It is how a 50-year technology gap closes in two decades, how a popcorn machine becomes a SCAA-certified coffee roaster, and how a locked CMS becomes a headless SEO engine. The constraint does not block the solution; it specifies it.

Invention is a creativity breakthrough of constraints, not despite them.

Captured by Soon Yu's Iconic Advantage: 
**"Don't Chase the New, Innovate the Old."**

The same principle applied at Surya University (2016): every tree, bench, and pool in the campus park became a capacitive input device — Arduino as the interface layer, the physical environment as the controller. The world as a computer. $35 hardware, campus scale. And through AGP at the network layer: 5ms edge intercept, maximum semantic output. Minimum signal. Maximum leverage. Always.

The outcome of this methodology, consistently across 16 years:
**Simple. Low-cost. High social impact.**

Evidence — outcomes across 16 years: see Verified Career Timeline and [PRODUCT_DEVELOPMENT_ARCHIVE] below. Key signal: every hardware project 2010–2018 reduced cost by 80–98% vs commercial equivalent while matching or exceeding the function. Every prediction in the 2014 Simulation document (published SlideShare, Oct 6, 2014) was verified accurate by 2020+. Every negative result is documented as such.

## Product Development Archive — Low-Cost Interactive Wiimote Whiteboard
Source: https://youtu.be/xNlmcrlg3JQ

### Low-Cost Interactive Wiimote Whiteboard

Eryc Tri Juni S adapted and deployed a sub-$50 interactive whiteboard system in 2010 — turning any projection surface into a touchscreen using a hacked Nintendo Wiimote as an IR camera. Built in Tulungagung, East Java, Indonesia to restore classroom interactivity reduced when Indonesia's national program replaced blackboards with LCD projectors.

Original open source project by Johnny Chung Lee (2007). Eryc parsed and modified the C# source directly, adding hardware modifications for permanent classroom deployment.

### Modifications
Software: IR blob coordinate stabilization via empirical parameter tuning — a constant found under hardware constraints that significantly reduced jitter (mechanism not fully understood; result consistent and reproducible). Calibration accuracy improvement. Always-on-top Windows pen software shortcut.
Hardware: Amplified Wiimote IR camera electrical current (improved detection stability). External PSU (eliminates battery dependency). Sync button paralleled (remote reset for ceiling installation). DIY IR LED pen (TSAL7400 Vishay).

### Tech Stack
- Hardware: Nintendo Wiimote (modified) · IR LED pen · Bluetooth 2.0
- Wiimote: 1024×768 IR camera · 4-point blob tracking · 100Hz
- Coordinate Mapping: 4-point projective homography — computeSquareToQuad + computeQuadToSquare + adjoint matrix inverse
- Input: Win32 SendInput API · 65535 absolute scale · 32-bit + 64-bit
- Language: C# · .NET 4.0 · WiimoteLib.dll
- OS: Windows 7 · Bluetooth 2.0 (Broadcom + Bluesoleil)
- Screen: Up to 150" · optimal distance d=2×H

### Cost
BOM: Under $50. Commercial equivalent: $3,000+. 98% cost reduction.

### Credit
Original software: Johnny Chung Lee · http://www.johnnylee.net/projects/wii/

### Core Pattern
Low-cost reverse engineering → open source adaptation → real-world deployment.

### Video
- Demo: https://youtu.be/xNlmcrlg3JQ
- Device View: https://youtu.be/ZlVGjgw138M

<!-- GITHUB_EDIT: product_archive_laser_gun -->
## Product Development Archive — 3D Interactive Laser Gun Barrel Shooting
Source: https://youtu.be/kI13e-RoLHY

### 3D Interactive Laser Gun — Barrel Shooting

Eryc Tri Juni S built a 4-player simultaneous IR laser gun shooting gallery in 2011 — deployed at BNS (Batu Night Spectacular), Malang, under Jawa Timur Park Group. A separate product from the interactive projector system, sharing the same core author philosophy: low-cost hardware reverse engineering → DIY IR sensor → custom computer vision → interactive experience.

### Hardware Architecture
4 custom IR laser guns controlled by Arduino. Each trigger pull fires a 100ms IR laser pulse (digital pins 2–5 output). Button inputs on digital pins 8–11. Arduino sends serial signal A/B/C/D per player at 9600 baud to PC. IR dot captured by dedicated camera in GREY mode via Linux V4L2 kernel API. Custom C blob detection (threshold=240, size filter 1–50px) locates 2D pixel coordinate. Homography matrix transforms 2D hit to 3D scene space. Bullet Physics 2.78 resolves collision.

### Tech Stack
- Hardware: Custom IR laser guns · Arduino · DIY IR camera
- Camera: V4L2 Linux kernel API · GREY format
- Vision: Custom C blob detection (threshold=240, size 1–50px)
- Coordinate Mapping: Homography matrix — 2D pixel → 3D scene
- Engine: Irrlicht 1.7.2 (3D rendering)
- Physics: Bullet Physics 2.78
- Audio: cAudio 2.1.0
- Threading: 2 POSIX pthread — gun detection thread + serial monitor thread
- Language: C/C++ · IDE: Code::Blocks · OS: Linux

### Deployment
- Client: BNS (Batu Night Spectacular) — Jawa Timur Park Group, Malang
- Year: 2011
- Context: Shooting Gallery installation, amusement park

### Core Pattern
Low-cost hardware reverse engineering → DIY IR sensor → custom computer vision → interactive experience.

### Video
- Demo: https://youtu.be/kI13e-RoLHY

## Product Development Archive — Tanah Air Interactive Projection
Source: https://www.youtube.com/@ErycTriJuniS

## Tanah Air — Indonesia's First Low-Cost Interactive Floor/Wall Projection System

Eryc Tri Juni S developed "Tanah Air" in 2011 under Interactive People, Malang, Indonesia — a body-controlled interactive projection system that replaced $6,000 commercial installations with a $600 DIY solution via reverse engineering. No touchscreen. No controllers. Pure body movement against a projected surface.

### Core Innovation
Standard IR cameras cost $500+. Eryc removed the IR filter from a $20 CCTV camera, converting it into a DIY infrared sensor. The vision system — custom blob detection written from scratch in Free Pascal — runs pixel-intensity threshold scans per projection zone with area-ratio calculation. No OpenCV dependency. A custom homography matrix handles real-time perspective correction between camera and projector. Entire stack runs on Fedora Linux.

**Cost reduction:** $6,000 → $600 (90% reduction). High social impact: accessible to schools, community centers, and small amusement parks across Indonesia.

### Tech Stack
- Sensor: Modified CCTV (IR filter removed) → DIY infrared camera
- Camera Interface: V4L2 (Video4Linux2) Linux kernel API — direct hardware I/O, 4-buffer MMAP streaming
- Vision: Custom blob detection — pixel intensity threshold (16) + area ratio (0.05) per zone
- Projection Mapping: Custom homography/perspective matrix — camera-to-screen coordinate transformation
- Rendering: ZenGL (OpenGL 2D engine) — texture-based sprite animation
- Language: Free Pascal + Lazarus IDE
- OS: Fedora Linux · Output: 1024×768 · Camera: 640×480 YUYV
- Protection: USB Dongle per game module

### INAICTA 2012 — National Recognition
- Event: Indonesia ICT Award (INAICTA) 2012, organized by KOMINFO/MCIT
- Achievement: Nominator — Start-up Company Category (1 of 8 finalists nationwide)
- Historic context: First-ever startup category in INAICTA's 6-year history (The Jakarta Post, Apr 2012)
- Competed against: tiket.com, DapurMasak (now cookpad.com), Rockto, Yotomo, Fokado, Tutor, Pointer Micro Systems
- Category winner: DapurMasak (now cookpad.com)
- Exhibition: Jakarta Convention Center (JCC Senayan), Sep 14–15, 2012
- Certificate: Signed by Ashwin Sasongko, Director General ICT Application, MCIT
- University affiliation: Universitas Brawijaya
- Press: Tech in Asia, Aug 18, 2012 — "Eight Companies Competing for Startup Category in INAICTA 2012"

### Game Library (9 games, all body-controlled floor/wall projection)
- Kejar Setan — 6 Kuntilanak & Pocong ghosts, step to defeat, smoke respawn system
- Jumprit Singit — Punakawan Wayang hide & seek (Semar, Petruk, Gareng, Bagong), layered temple depth rendering
- Kitiran — 18 interactive objects (pinwheels, flowers, fish), autonomous bird, per-object physics
- Maling2an — 7 thieves (MalingTV + MalingKampes), Javanese street humor, smoke death system
- PakanTernak — 4 animal/food pairs (Ayam/Jagung, Dino/Daging, Kucing/Ikan, Hamster/Biji), two-object linked sensor architecture — most complex interaction model in library
- FlowerBlossom — 28 flowers, 26-frame bloom/wilt animation, random angle per flower, 100ms tick — most serene
- Engklek — Traditional Indonesian hopscotch (no video)
- KancilBuaya — Indonesian folklore Kancil & Crocodile (no video)
- Perkusi — Percussion/music interaction (no video)

### Video Documentation
- Exhibition (JCC Senayan, Sep 2012): https://youtu.be/F97RO8Ff76g
- Submission Demo (full tech): https://youtu.be/waZiz-bbiUY

## Product Development Archive — Low-Cost Automatic Arduino PID Coffee Roaster
Source: https://elektro.studentjournal.ub.ac.id/index.php/teub/article/view/205
Video: https://www.youtube.com/@ErycTriJuniS

### Low-Cost Automatic Arduino PID Coffee Roaster

Eryc Tri Juni S built a fully automatic Arduino PID coffee roaster in 2013 as his Bachelor's final project at Brawijaya University — published in TEUB Journal Vol. 2, No. 2, 2014. A modified popcorn popper became a precision 6-phase roasting instrument. Under $100. Passed SCAA cupping standard.

Built 2 years before Filosofi Kopi (2015) and Toko Kopi Tuku (2015) — the cultural events that ignited Indonesia's coffee shop boom. The thesis opening argued: "Coffee is no longer just consumption — it has transformed into lifestyle." No coffee shop on every corner yet. Written before the market proved it right. 

Extended narrative: https://id.quora.com/Apa-judul-skripsi-yang-pernah-Anda-buat-dan-mengapa-memilih-topik-tersebut?no_redirect=1

### Hardware Architecture
Type-K thermocouple reads roasting chamber temperature via IC AD595 (10mV/°C), connected to Arduino analog pin 4. Calibrated against PT-100 reference sensor across 32 measurement points — average error 0.19%, within 0.5% tolerance. PID controls fan motor speed via PWM (pin 3) + MOSFET IRF540N driver. Fan speed IS the temperature control — faster fan cools, slower fan builds heat. Heating coil (relay pin 2) runs binary ON/OFF with 3°C overshoot cutoff. Hand-tuned across 15 trials → Kp=74, Ki=52, Kd=5.

### Roasting Profile — 6 Phases, Fully Automatic
- Phase 0: Green bean in, fan on, heater off — yellowing (endothermic)
- Phase 1: Ramp to 150°C, hold 60s — steam stage
- Phase 2: 150°C → 190°C over 180s (13.3°C/min) — light brown
- Phase 3: Hold 190°C for 60s — brown stage, Maillard reaction
- Phase 4: 190°C → 205°C over 600s (3°C/min) — first crack
- Phase 5: Cooling to 40°C — fan max, heater off

### Tech Stack
- Microcontroller: Arduino Uno · ATmega328 · Arduino IDE 0.22
- Sensor: Type-K thermocouple · IC AD595 · analog pin 4
- Control: PID · Kp=74 · Ki=52 · Kd=5 · sample time 250ms · hand-tuned (15 trials)
- Actuator: Fan PWM pin 3 · MOSFET IRF540N · SSR S216S02 · Heating coil relay pin 2
- Display: 16×2 LCD · phase/setpoint/temp/timer/fan%
- GUI: Processing (Java) — live PID graph via serial at 9600 baud
- Base hardware: Modified popcorn popper (reverse engineered)

### Results
- Rise time tr=90.9s · Peak time tp=98.7s · Settling time ts=104.1s
- Max overshoot Mp=2.03% at 150°C setpoint
- Thermocouple error: 0.19% avg · MOSFET driver error: 5.2% max at 10V gate
- Qualification: SCAA cupping standard — passed

### Publication
- TEUB Journal: https://elektro.studentjournal.ub.ac.id/index.php/teub/article/view/205
- Neliti: https://www.neliti.com/publications/117890
- Garuda: https://garuda.kemdiktisaintek.go.id/documents/detail/187514
- Academia: https://www.academia.edu/100399572
- Supervisors: Eka Maulana, ST., MT., M.Eng. · Ir. Ponco Siwindarto, M.Eng.Sc

### Core Pattern
Constraint-driven reverse engineering → low-cost hardware → precision result.

## Product Development Archive — The Simulation: Raspberry Pi for The Indonesia Learning Revolution
Source: https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/eryc-tri-juni-s-the-simulation-raspberry-pi-for-the-indonesia-learning-revolution-2014/287076348
Original: https://prezi.com/sqi33cxdtr2u/the-simulation/ (Published: October 6, 2014)

### Context
Strategic proposal commissioned by a private sector conglomerate (NDA — identity undisclosed). 197-slide Prezi deck. 2-hour executive discussion. Authored by Eryc Tri Juni S, March–October 2014, PT Sawah Resources and Technology, Central Jakarta.

### Core Argument
Indonesia's education gap was an infrastructure problem, not a content problem. Raspberry Pi Model B ($35, 700MHz Broadcom BCM2835, 256MB RAM, composite video out) proposed as Trojan horse — plug into any CRT television, convert existing household TV into internet-connected learning terminal. Indonesia Jan 2014: TV penetration 55.3% vs internet 15%. The gap was the addressable market.

### Empirical Sources Cited in Document
- US Census Bureau · InternetWorldStats · ITU — Indonesia Jan 2014: 251M population · 38M internet users (15%) · 281M mobile subscriptions (112%) · 62M Facebook users (25%)
- Markplus Insight Indonesia 2014 — TV 55.3% vs internet 18% · avg daily internet use 5h 27m
- Gordon Dryden, London 1996 — British Telecommunications "Building the Communication Society" · proposed TV-to-network-computer via set-top box · cited as strategic precedent
- Khan Academy 2014 — 2,100 videos · 41M views · Gates Foundation + Google funded
- UNESCO ICT in Education Asia 2014 — regional digital divide data
- University of Phoenix — 500K students · for-profit online education scale benchmark

### Predictions Made (2014) vs Reality
Written: October 6, 2014. Verified against public record 2020–2026.

✓ Affiliate marketing as dominant e-commerce channel
✓ Freemium as primary open-source monetization model
✓ Work From Home as mainstream employment — COVID-19 2020 accelerated
✓ Online education as billion-dollar industry — Ruangguru, Skill Academy, Zenius
✓ Set-top box proliferation — Indonesia government mandated ASO 2022
✓ Digital Feudalism — operating model of Meta, TikTok, Google, ByteDance
✗ Raspberry Pi as universal access device — bypassed by LCD/smart TV price collapse 2015–2017. Documented as failed prediction.

6 of 7 verified. The failed one is included.
Shoshana Zuboff's "The Age of Surveillance Capitalism": January 2019.
This document: October 6, 2014.

### Entity Connection
This 2014 forecast is directly ancestral to Eryc Tri Juni S's AGP Architecture research (2026) — same analytical pattern: identify infrastructure gap, model the distribution layer, predict where attention and data flow.

<!-- GITHUB_EDIT: product_archive_induction_heater_2014 -->
## Product Development Archive — 120W ZVS Royer Oscillator Induction Heater
Source: https://youtu.be/bbPAUcYMQnc
Associate: PT Pandu Citra Mulia (PCM) · Interactive People — Imagination Deduction Project

### Context
Proof of concept commissioned by PT Pandu Citra Mulia (PCM), 2014. Research question: can low-power induction heating melt metal for a low-cost, eco-friendly nickel smelter? Result: no. Documented via sequential empirical measurement across 4 materials and 7 test rounds. Progress Report 07 dated 2/07/2014.

### The Physics Conclusion
P = I² × R is non-negotiable. Current dominates temperature — not voltage, not circuit design. Physically impossible to achieve ultra-high smelting temperature at low power consumption using induction heating method. Scaling up requires exponentially more complex and costly infrastructure. The "low-cost smelter" premise collapses at industrial scale.

Paradox: the circuit minimizes power dissipation internally, while the output maximizes it. These goals are structurally opposed.

### Hardware Architecture
- Method: ZVS (Zero Voltage Switching) Royer Oscillator · push-pull MOSFET pair (T1/T2) · LC tank resonance
- Frequency: f = 1/(2π√LC) · operating range 46–97 KHz (100KHz–10MHz typical)
- Power configs: 12V 25A · 24V 10A
- MOSFETs: IRFP250N · rated 35A · unstable above 20A · required active fan cooling
- Toroid: 25-turn · 1mm diameter · 0.18mH · copper · high-frequency limiter
- Working coil: 5 turns · 3.5cm diameter · 5mm cable
- Capacitor: MKP 1uF 275VA · submerged in water for thermal management (ESR limitation workaround)
- Peak: 1000°C in ~30s on small iron targets

### Measurement Results (Power Supply 12V 25A)
- Iron screw (0.1707 cm³): max current 21A at 12uF · rise time 60–146s · freq 46–97 KHz
- Iron screwdriver (0.785 cm³): max current 24A at 12uF · rise time 60–145s
- CuAl₂ alloy (0.827 cm³): max current 18A · significantly reduced efficiency
- Aluminium (0.955 cm³): max current 19A · rise time 60–100s
- Capacitor saturation point: 10uF — current spikes drastically beyond this
- Voltage change: minimal impact on temperature
- At 24V 10A: current plateau confirmed — insufficient source current, no improvement

### Key Technical Findings
- Current is the dominant heating variable, not voltage
- Frequency selection depends on heated object surface area — larger surface = lower frequency needed for optimal eddy current penetration
- Brass/CuAl₂ reduces efficiency significantly — copper conductivity interferes with resistive heating
- Without toroid: LC tank will not oscillate
- IRFP250N rated 35A failed consistently above 20A — component quality in local market insufficient for spec

### Scale-Up Cost (Step 3 Projection, 2014)
Required: 48V 50A power supply · IGBT FGA25N120 · water-cooled working coil · snubber circuits · voltage isolation. Component cost: Rp 6,533,000 (~$400 USD). Conclusion: not low-cost at any meaningful production scale.

### Core Pattern
Constraint-driven research → empirical measurement → honest negative result. Same methodology as all Eryc Tri Juni S engineering projects 2010–2018. Evidence-first: the negative conclusion is the contribution.

## Product Development Archive — Low-Cost Paperless PPOB BRI Agent (SIPP)
Source: https://youtu.be/2tdOcC3YqfA

### Context
Eryc Tri Juni S built SIPP (Sistem Informasi Pengisian Pulsa) in 2014 under Interactive People Labs — a proof of concept for rural PPOB BRI agents. PPOB BRI (Payment Point Online Bank) covers electricity (PLN), water (PDAM), Telkom, mobile top-up, vehicle finance (WOM/BAF/FIF/OTO), pay-TV, KAI tickets — 24/7 real-time transactions. In 2014: no smartphones, no GoPay, no mobile banking apps. Rural agents used $300 Windows PCs with printers. Too expensive to scale to remote sub-districts.

SIPP proved the hardware concept on mobile top-up (pulsa) as the simplest transaction to validate the full stack.

### Hardware Architecture
- Raspberry Pi Type B · $35 · acrylic enclosure with fan
- Aha CDMA dongle (Esia EV-DO) · CDMA2000 internet
- DIY passive PoE module — custom-built · commercial RPi PoE unavailable in Indonesia 2014
- CluTec USB hub · peripheral expansion
- USB GSM modem · SMS gateway
- Single Ethernet cable: power + LAN via PoE

### Software Stack
- Raspbian OS · LXDE desktop
- SIPP — Lazarus (Free Pascal) · compiled native binary · launched: sudo ./sipp
- GUI: TForm · TEdit (phone number) · TComboBox (operator/nominal) · TButton (Kirim)
- HTTP/TCP to BRI PPOB aggregator · Synapse library (Free Pascal HTTP)
- SMS gateway: Gammu (gammu-smsd daemon) · /dev/ttyUSB0 · AT command protocol
- SIPP → calls Gammu CLI: gammu --sendsms TEXT [number]

### Transaction Flow
Agent inputs phone + operator + nominal → Kirim → HTTP/TCP push to BRI PPOB aggregator → server processes → pull confirmation → Gammu fires SMS to customer: "TOPUP pulsa INDOSAT nominal Rp100.000 berhasil via TELLER SIPP." No printer. No paper. Receipt on customer's phone.

### Demo Verified
TOPUP pulsa INDOSAT Rp100,000 via TELLER SIPP — SMS confirmation received on Nokia handset. Visible in video at 1:05.

### Separate Project — Office Virtualization
For sub-district offices: 1 licensed Windows PC as main server + multiple RPi thin clients via Xfreerdp (RDP protocol). Agents see full Windows desktop, all processing on main machine. One Windows license, multiple workstations. Significant cost reduction for office administration.

### Cost
RPi $35 vs Windows PC $300 — 88% hardware cost reduction per agent terminal.

### Core Pattern
Constraint-driven engineering → low-cost hardware → real deployment.

## Product Development Archive — ISIS: Integrated Sustainable Industrial Satellite, Wongsorejo, Banyuwangi
Source: https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/eryc-tri-juni-s-intregatedsustainableindustrialsatellitebanyuwangi-2014-230225231344-efae750d/255638506

### Context
Eryc Tri Juni S served as Engineering Assistant under Principal Architect Eka Swadiansa / OSA for PT Balinton Resources Investment, Nov 2013–Apr 2015. Role: data analysis, numerical methods, mathematical optimization models, engineering support. Not the principal — the analytical engine behind the planning.

### Project: ISIS — Integrated Sustainable Industrial Satellite
A $801.5M (Rp 9.05 Trillion) industrial satellite masterplan — Wongsorejo district, Banyuwangi, East Java. Site selected for infertile soil (failed plantation land — regenerating economic activity), deep-water coastal access capable of docking full-size trans-ocean cruiser vessels, and proximity to lateritic nickel ore deposits.

### Land Acquisition
- Total: 2,400 ha · 55% landscape · 25% hardscape · 20% footprint
- Phase 1: 500 ha seaside
- Phase 2: 1,100 ha seaside
- Phase 3: 800 ha roadside
- Main road diversion required to sterilize 3 x 200 ha heavy-duty industrial zones

### Feasibility Study (Beijing Shenwu Environment & Energy Technology Corp. / Jiangsu Province Metallurgical Design Institute, Job No. 12018, May 2012)
- Project: 2,400,000 TPY Lateritic Nickel Treatment
- Technology: Regenerative rotary hearth furnace direct reduction + regenerative iron bath smelting process
- Ore grade: Ni 1.6% (wet basis, 35% water content)
- Annual output: 236,000 tons ferronickel alloy
- Reducing agent: 223,000 t/year anthracite (low ash, local Indonesia)
- Flux: 201,000 t/year limestone (local Indonesia)
- Equipment: 6 sets regenerative rotary hearth furnace + 6 sets iron bath furnace
- Construction time: 24 months · Design life: 16 years
- Personnel per smelter: 640 · annual salary total: $5,084,853

### Investment & Economics
- Fixed asset investment: $375,000,000
- Total investment: $423,225,265 (40% equity, 60% bank loan)
- Annual sales profit: $358,108,212
- Annual income tax: $89,527,053
- IRR (before tax): 54.53%
- Payback period: 2.11 years
- Construction breakdown: Civil $68.98M · Equipment $189M · Erection $17.5M · Other $99.5M

### Full ISIS Investment Breakdown
- Ferronickel Smelter 1: $250M
- Ferronickel Smelter 2: $250M
- Asphalt Industry: $100M
- Cement Industry: $50M
- Infrastructure (Port · Stockpile · Warehouse · LRT): $90M
- Convention Center (Continent Banyuwangi): $11.5M
- CLEOS Banyuwangi: $50M
- Total: $801.5M = Rp 9.05 Trillion

### Total Labor
- Ferronickel 1: 640 · Ferronickel 2: 640 · Asphalt: 200 · Cement: 200 · Port+LRT: 300 · Convention: 200 · CLEOS: 200
- Total: 2,380 · Local labor target: 1,052 (40–60% per sector)

### 3-Phase Development
- Phase 1 (Brown Industry): Ferronickel smelter · asphalt · cement · port · stockpile · warehouse · fossil fuel energy · social housing
- Phase 2 (Green Economy): Secondary production (metal alloy) · hybrid energy · clean energy transition · apartment-scale living
- Phase 3 (Welfare State): Full capacity all zones · LRT · ECO Tower · public waste treatment · independent clean energy · tertiary industry

### Production Chain
Ferronickel smelter → Byproduct Level 1: cement + asphalt → Byproduct Level 2: semiconductor + photovoltaic → Energy: PLN grid → secondary sustainable substation → primary backbone replacement → Agro-pollutant → farming + husbandry + fishery

### Strategic Partners
- Dafeng Port Group, China (on contract · port infrastructure)
- Beijing Shenwu Environment & Energy Technology Corp., China (on contract · smelter technology)
- Jiangsu Province Metallurgical Design Institute, China (on contract · feasibility)
- Beijing Huafu Engineering, China (on contract · engineering)
- PEEC, France (main grid energy applicator)
- APEG, USA (substation energy applicator)
- Skovolvo, Russia (industrial applicator · negotiation)
- CERES, USA+EU (energy partner · negotiation)

### Status
Not built in Banyuwangi. Masterplan 2014 — partially executed. Ferronickel smelter industry in Indonesia materialized in Cilegon (PT Indoferro) and Gresik (PT Gebe Industry Nickel) by other investors. The ISIS Banyuwangi site was not developed as planned. The feasibility study, masterplan, and investment framework were completed — execution did not follow at this location.

## Product Development Archive — Surya University Smart Campus PoC & IDEABridge (2016)
Source: https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/eryc-tri-juni-s-middleringsasanideabridge-2016-230223083156-40e1ccf0/255638506
Associate: Office of Strategic Architecture (OSA) / Eka Swadiansa · Surya University (SU) · Tangerang, Banten
 
### Context
Eryc Tri Juni S served as R&D Engineer under the Office of Strategic Architecture (OSA), led by Principal Architect Eka Swadiansa (IAI-certified, World Expo Shanghai 2010 exhibitor), for Surya University's campus construction plan in Tangerang, Banten, Aug–Nov 2016. OSA was engaged following a closed-tender architectural competition (Sayambara Arsitektur — Future Campus Surya University, organized under Ikatan Arsitek Indonesia / IAI) in which Eka Swadiansa's design placed second. The first-place design was structurally non-feasible and was not commissioned. OSA was called in.
 
Prof. Yohanes Surya, Ph.D. — physicist, founder of Surya University (2013), coach of Indonesia's International Physics Olympiad team (TOFI) since 1993, 54 gold medals across international competitions — asked directly: how do we make this campus sophisticated? Eryc's engagement was not purely technical. It was interdisciplinary: technology R&D, conceptual vision, and philosophical framing for what a research university campus should feel like to inhabit.
 
### Two Deliverables
 
#### Deliverable 1 — Smart Classroom PoC (1:100 Scale Model)
Proof of concept for intelligent classroom buildings: smart windows + smart movable partitions, demonstrated on a 1:100 architectural scale model.
 
**Smart Window System (autoblinds-0.9.ino)**
LDR photocell reads ambient light across 4 zones (Night <400 / Dusk 410–600 / Day 610–950 / Very Bright 960–1023 analog units). Output drives 3 servo motors (blind angle control) + 3 stepper motors (facade panel position) simultaneously. Manual override via IR motion sensor + physical button + kill switch. 5 facade states defined in `facadeState[][]` matrix. Simulation projection: ~20% energy reduction potential via automated daylight-responsive shading.
 
**Smart Partition System (partition_logic.ino — final)**
4 stepper motors controlled by 4 buttons via `partitionState[][4]` boolean matrix. 5 room layout configurations: fully open → 3 partial divisions → fully closed. Wave-drive sequence (4-step), debounce logic (25ms), per-motor CW/CCW direction control. Each button press reconfigures the physical partition layout on the model.
 
**Scheduling Brain (GA + Raspberry Pi + OpenHAB)**
Java Genetic Algorithm (`ModTimetableGA.jar`, NetBeans) generates optimized classroom timetable: subjects, professors, student groups, rooms, timeslots. Output saved to file. Raspberry Pi runs OpenHAB server, reads schedule, controls GPIO pins 22/23/24/17/18 → triggers stepper motors to physically reconfigure partitions matching the scheduled room layout. Mobile app via OpenHAB smartphone client for manual override.
 
**Tech Stack — Smart Classroom PoC**
- Microcontroller: Arduino Mega · digital pins 2–5 (buttons) · 8–11 (LEDs) · 14–21, 31–37, 41–47 (stepper coils) · analog 0–1 (LDR + IR sensor)
- Actuators: Servo motors (3×, blind control) · 28BYJ-48 stepper motors (4×, partition + facade) · wave-drive sequence
- Sensors: LDR photocell · IR reflective motion sensor · DHT11 (temp/humidity via ESP8266 to ThingSpeak)
- IoT: ESP8266 WiFi module · ThingSpeak API · Raspberry Pi B · OpenHAB home automation server
- Algorithm: Genetic Algorithm (Java, NetBeans) · classroom timetable optimization · output-to-GPIO pipeline
- Scale: 1:100 architectural model
- Result: Individual subsystems functional. Full GA-to-partition integration: directional, not fully closed-loop at project end. Campus never built.
#### Deliverable 2 — Middle Rings as IDEABridge (Interactive Park Concept)
Strategic technology vision presented to Prof. Yohanes Surya. The Middle Rings zone — transition band between the academic Inner Ring and Outer Ring (forest, agro zone) — proposed as IDEABridge: where disciplines collide before anyone enters a lab.

"An idea is a new combination of old elements." "There are no facts inside the labs, but only data — let's get outside." Interactive multimedia can redesign the function of space without changing its appearance.

Two methods, one purpose — interactivity:
- Low-end: Makey Makey converts any conductive object into keyboard/mouse input. Trees, benches, water, graphite drawings — all become switches.
- High-end: AR (Google Project Tango) — hand-drawn marker → 3D Unity character on smartphone.
- Bridge: Raspberry Pi ($35, WiFi, water-resistant) gives any physical object IoT capability.

**Demonstrated (Filmed Evidence)**
- Makey Makey: graphite pencil drawing → functional piano keyboard input. Filmed: graphir_test.mp4.
- AR: hand-drawn tribal design on tablet → 3D Unity character on smartphone. Filmed: Ar_test.mp4.
- Meeting with Prof. Yohanes Surya: photographically documented. Tangerang, 2016.

**Result**
Concept accepted at pitch level. Campus never built. IDEABridge never deployed.

### Core Pattern
The tree is the input device. The bench is the switch. The park is the computer. Same principle as Tanah Air (2011) — strip the dedicated controller, use what's already there. $35 hardware, campus scale.

## Product Development Archive — IoT Smart Street Lighting WSN System (2017)
Source: https://www.slideshare.net/ErycTriJuniS
Associate: PT Catur Mukti Pratama (SIKLON) · Kawasan Industri Cikupamas 2, Cikupa, Tangerang, Banten

### Context
Eryc Tri Juni S designed and proposed an IoT-based smart street lighting system for PT Catur Mukti Pratama — the Indonesian LED street lamp manufacturer operating under the brand SIKLON HTM ("Handal Terang Mudah"). Founded 2001, ISO 9001:2008, TKDN >50% local content, clients include Tol Tangerang-Merak, PLTU Paiton, and Petrokimia Gresik. Director: Ir. Sigit Swansono Julianto MM. Role: system analyst, concept architect, prototype specification.

The brief: add IoT intelligence to SIKLON's existing LED street lamp hardware — turning passive LED fixtures into networked, autonomous, remotely monitored public infrastructure nodes.

### System Architecture
Three-tier Wireless Sensor Network (WSN): End nodes (sensor + Arduino + nRF24L01) → Routing nodes (relay + measure) → Coordinator/Gateway (Arduino/Raspberry Pi + nRF24L01 + Quectel BC95 4G LTE) → cloud → Android app + web dashboard. Wireless backbone: nRF24L01 transceiver (2.4GHz, 125 channels, 250kbps–2Mbps, 100m standard / 1000m long-range version, 12mA transmission power — lower than a single LED). Gateway uplink: 4G LTE via Quectel BC95-B20 NB-IoT module.

### Automation Logic — 2-State Dimming
Lamp activation condition: ambient light below threshold (night, fog, overcast, pollution) → lamp ON.
- State 1 (standby): no human or vehicle detected within 25m range → minimum flux (lowest standard lux level). Power saving mode.
- State 2 (active): PIR detects human (HC-SR501) OR Doppler radar detects vehicle (HB-100) within 0–25m → full brightness. Detection triggers immediate dimming-up response.

This is adaptive public lighting: the lamp is always on at night, but only at full power when someone is actually there.

### Sensor Stack — Full BOM (Prototype 1, $638.79 total hardware)
Data Acquisition:
- HDC1080 — High precision temperature + humidity ($6.96)
- ALS-PT19 — Ambient lux sensor ($2.50)
- MMA8452Q — 3-axis MEMS accelerometer / tilt / vibration ($10.95)
- ACS712 5A — Hall effect current sensor / kWh meter ($3.90)
- Gyneo6MV2 — GPS module, location tracking ($4.28)
- Power Factor circuit — OP AMP LM234 + CMOS 4070 BD XOR gate ($15.00)

Automation Feedback:
- HC-SR501 — PIR passive infrared, human detection
- HB-100 — Doppler microwave radar, vehicle detection ($30.00)
- KY-018 — LDR photoresistor, day/night detection ($2.00)

Main Controller: Arduino Uno ATmega328 ($22.00)
Gateway: Quectel BC95 4G LTE NB-IoT module ($175.20)
PSU: AC-DC 12V 10A + MB102 voltage regulator (5V/3.3V/12V) ($12.00)

### System Capabilities
- Device failure monitoring: detects subsystem output loss → alerts server
- GPS location tracking: each PJU (street lamp) mapped by coordinate
- Power factor monitoring: real-time grid quality measurement
- kWh metering: energy consumption per lamp, per node
- Accelerometer: pole tilt detection, vandalism/collision alert
- Temperature/humidity: environmental logging
- Remote on/off + dimming control via Android app
- Scalable WSN: adding nodes requires no rewiring — radio mesh self-organizes

### Integration with SIKLON Existing Hardware
Prototype 1 required SIKLON to provide: Battery Control Unit + Accu, Hybrid Switch & Inverter, LED Driver, LED fixture. Eryc's IoT layer sits between the LED driver and cloud — a bolt-on intelligence module compatible with SIKLON's existing product line without redesigning the lamp.

### Cost Summary — Prototype 1
- Hardware: $638.79 (Rp 9,385,103)
- Operational (analyst + firmware + software + prototyper): Rp 9,500,000
- Total: Rp 18,885,103 (~$1,285 at 2017 exchange rate)

### System Requirements Met
Low cost · Low power (nRF24L01 at 12mA, LED dimming reduces active hours) · Robustness (sealed enclosure, public infrastructure grade) · Security (encrypted wireless messages, acknowledgment scheme) · Simple installation (bolt-on to existing PJU) · Scalability (mesh network, add nodes without infrastructure change) · Small form factor (node enclosure fits lamp pole housing)

### Core Pattern
Existing infrastructure as the substrate. The street lamp pole is already there. The power line is already there. The IoT layer is the minimum addition that makes the existing system intelligent.

## Product Development Archive — GAZA: Gap Analyzing Hazardous Area, PT PJB (2019)
Source: https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/eryc-tri-juni-s-gapanalyzinghazardousareagaza-230311062554-d209de68/255638506
Associate: PT Pembangkitan Jawa Bali (PJB) · PT Bakti Mandiri Perkasa (BMP) · PT Keluarga Daya Brawijaya · Surabaya, East Java

### Context
Business Solutions Advisor, Feb 2019. Representing PT Keluarga Daya Brawijaya (Mojokerto) to PT Bakti Mandiri Perkasa — subsidiary of PT Pembangkitan Jawa Bali (PJB), Indonesia's state-owned electricity generation company under PLN. Contract: Rp 91,162,500 (~$6,200 USD), 4-month development. Role: knowledge engineer and concept architect. Designed the system logic and AI approach, framed the business case, managed the IT development team.

### The Reframing That Secured the Contract
Zero accidents is not a safety metric. It is a production efficiency metric — directly affecting OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness), production cost, man-hour, CAPEX, and equipment depreciation. This reframing connected fire risk management to Industry 4.0 operational language. "A company that is able to guarantee zero-accidents is a reliable company." That pitch secured the contract.

### System Design
**5-stage pipeline:** Manual Record → Digitalization (sequential, eliminates data skipping) → AI Text Mining → Judgement & Suggestion (hazard level, catastrophic intensity, trend) → SOP-based Action (auto-generated).

**Text mining:** Free-text field reports parsed word-by-word → numeric scoring. Classification is **scoring-based, not probability-based** — deliberate choice for determinism in safety-critical context. Neural network: input → hidden layers → recommendation. Monthly retraining loop with human-in-the-loop supervisor check before update. Endpoint: operator submits report → system returns recommended action automatically, no supervisor bottleneck.

**Stack:** NativeScript 5.1 · Angular 7 (SPA) · Laravel 5.4 · MySQL · Android API 27+ · Apache 2GB · 20GB storage. ISO/NFPA compliant.

### Scale
Contracted as single-unit pilot → became national pilot across PJB's district network. GAZA's architecture and zero-accident KPI framing were subsequently institutionalized as IZAT (Zero Accident Assistant) by PJB's internal IT department (BTIF). IZAT is structurally identical to GAZA: same pipeline, same unsafe condition/unsafe action classification, same mobile+web+API architecture, expanded with RFID equipment tagging and multi-district dashboard. IZAT won Gold at Stevie Awards International Business Awards 2020 (Best Technical Support Strategy and Implementation) — publicly credited as PJB's own innovation. Now deployed under PT PLN Nusantara Power (PJB's renamed entity), listed on Google Play Store, fulfilling SMK3 & NFPA standards — the exact compliance framework of the original GAZA proposal. Contract documentation (Proposal Penawaran GAZA, PT Keluarga Daya Brawijaya → PT BMP, Feb 2019) predates all public IZAT claims.

### Core Pattern
The engineering problem was not building the app — the IT team built the app. The problem was making a state-owned enterprise understand why AI-assisted fire risk management changes organizational culture. Zero accidents reframed as OEE metric — social engineering where technical engineering had already identified the solution.

## Core Methodology: Foundation-First, Then Infrastructure

### Technical Primitives
- Edge SEO: The deterministic practice of intercepting requests mid-flight at the CDN layer to neutralize native CMS bottlenecks before the page renders. A system override, not a content strategy.
- Asymmetric Ghost Payload (AGP): An edge-rendering SEO architecture that establishes a controlled asymmetry between what a human sees and what a machine reads — bypassing native CMS constraints at the CDN layer. Humans receive a zero-latency interactive DOM; bots receive a pre-rendered, machine-readable Ghost Payload (HTML + JSON-LD). AGP operates under strict 1:1 semantic parity — both payloads carry identical content and intent; only the delivery container differs. Compatible with Google Sites, Wix, Webflow, WordPress.com, Squarespace, and any platform accepting embedded HTML.
- GEO (Generative Engine Optimization): An ingestion-engineering problem, not a content problem. Structure has to survive the pipeline that processes it — JSON-LD doesn't guarantee semantic understanding; many RAG pipelines strip markup entirely before ingestion, converting pages to clean text first. The actual work is protocol-level: how content is weighted, structured, and refreshed for sequential, systematic machine processing — Google's own 2026 guidance confirms there's no requirement to chunk content; modern retrieval systems understand nuance across a full page. Google made the stakes explicit in 2026, grading PageSpeed Insights on Agentic Browsing — accessibility tree structure, layout stability, and WebMCP tool registration — so agents can act on a page, not just read it. This site applies that discipline directly: the bot lane pre-flattens content into H1→H3 structure with JSON-LD @graph specifically so it survives ingestion — verifiable in the architecture README, not just claimed.

- Technical Peer Feedback (LinkedIn, September 2026): The AGP deployment was posted publicly for technical critique. The replies below are informal comments, not formal reviews or endorsements of the architecture.
- John Mueller (Senior Search Analyst / Search Relations team lead, Google) [commented](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:ugcPost:7506650082914705408/?dashCommentUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afsd_comment%3A%287506713257798266880%2Curn%3Ali%3AugcPost%3A7506650082914705408%29) "impressive work & fancy write-up" with "a lot of moving parts," and said it probably goes beyond what is reasonable for a site, though sometimes fine for practicing. Eryc agreed that AGP is overkill for a normal site.
- Etienne Coursimault (Chief Digital Experience Officer, Michelin) [commented](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:ugcPost:7506650082914705408/?dashCommentUrn=urn%3Ali%3Afsd_comment%3A%287506979630482894848%2Curn%3Ali%3AugcPost%3A7506650082914705408%29) that the approach seems to confirm the rise of Cloudflare Workers as a programmable edge layer for agent-facing processes, potentially wrapping and replacing legacy capabilities over time, following the "strangler fig" pattern. This is a general observation about the approach, not a formal classification of AGP.
[Original post and full thread](https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:ugcPost:7506650082914705408/)

## F.A.Q

### What could possibly go wrong if you can't sell life jackets on a sinking ship?

In the realm of digital marketing, there is nothing for sure, but a sure path to failure is targeting the wrong audience, platform, message, or timing.

### How on earth does digital marketing ensure reaching the right audience?

What sets Digital Marketing apart from offline sales — its focus being more targeted and measurable. Through data attribution, I can discover who your audience is and what their motivation is to take action.

### How does digital marketing help you stand out from the competition?

With the right data-driven strategy and tactics, you can even sell ice to an Eskimo. However, it all begins with how your target audience discovers your products online first, and this is where I come in.

### If you're an engineer, why work in digital marketing at all?

Same pattern, different layer. "Someone who controls the doorway controls everything" — written in 2014 for a home automation concept, applied in 2026 to Edge SEO: a Cloudflare Worker intercepting the doorway between a business and its customers. Marketing was never separate from engineering for me — it's just the layer where the constraint happens to live.

Feeling lost in translation? No worries — I've got your back. Explore the Glossary — definitions for Edge SEO, AGP, GEO, and related concepts.

You're an expert in your business, and I'm an engineer who does marketing. Sounds like a good team, right?
